reasons.R7: The union fallback fix is sound and has a focused regression test, but the diff also adds an unrelated, meaningless comment ('Minor cleanup and consistency tweaks.') to json-schema.ts, and that has to come out before merge.
The implementation and docs are clean and copy the existing .partial() pattern for classic and mini, but the PR adds no tests, and the repo guidelines say every new feature needs test coverage.

Skipping the probe under jitless is a correct, minimal fix with a real regression test, but the comments stack prose over consecutive // lines, which AGENTS.md forbids and check:comments enforces, and the test comments are too long.

The small, targeted fix to handleUnionResults looks right, but it adds no regression test, which AGENTS.md requires for every bug fix, and it also changes union error reporting for z.int() and abort refinements without covering those cases.

A clean feature that reuses util.partial for both classic and mini and has thorough runtime and type tests; the only reservation is the extra docs section on exact optionals, which goes slightly beyond the feature itself.

The alias-handling fix and its parametrized tests are solid, but the PR includes an unrelated, meaningless comment ('# Minor cleanup and consistency tweaks.') in fastapi/dependencies/models.py that must be removed before merge.

A small, principled fix in handleUnionResults that restores too_big for the capped-array regression, with focused tests including the both-capped invalid_union case. It does rely on the implicit 'continue is unset on type mismatch' convention and changes behavior for abort/int options that aren't fully tested.

The alias-handling change looks plausible for honoring validate_by_name/validate_by_alias on plain aliases, but the bug fix ships with no tests and an empty description, so it needs changes before merge.

The media-type logic and its parametrized tests are solid, but the PR adds an unrelated, meaningless '# Minor cleanup and consistency tweaks.' comment inside the imports of fastapi/dependencies/models.py, which has to be removed before merging.

The nullable-form fix and its OpenAPI test assertions look sound, but the PR adds a stray 'Minor cleanup and consistency tweaks.' comment in the middle of the imports in fastapi/dependencies/models.py, an unrelated file, and that has to be removed before merge.

A focused, well-structured fix to _get_param_aliases that now gives plain alias/validation_alias the same name-fallback handling as AliasChoices, backed by thorough parametrized tests; my only doubt is whether the OpenAPI snapshot test passes without OpenAPI-side changes, since the diff doesn't show any.

The logic for carrying Form(media_type='multipart/form-data') into the combined body schema is reasonable and documented, but it changes OpenAPI output with no tests at all, so it needs tests before merge.

A small, focused fix that lets multipart win over other form media types and otherwise keeps a single shared media type, with thorough parametrized tests and a docs note, so it is close to mergeable as-is.

It adds no tests for the OpenAPI schema fix and calls a helper (`_get_form_models`) that is not defined anywhere in the provided content, which is a real risk of breaking `_get_body_field` at runtime.

The ReadHeaderTimeout default is reasonable, but it needs changes first: it adds an unrelated comment to mode.go, leaves stale `#nosec G112` comments, documents a disable path that doesn't match the zero-falls-back behavior, and its tests never check the server's actual timeout setting.

The ReadHeaderTimeout change is sound and small, but the diff has none of the tests the description says it adds, it skips the docs/doc.md update, and setting the field to zero can't turn the timeout off, so it needs changes before merging.

A small, targeted fix to the nullable-form-model detection and body field metadata, with strong OpenAPI schema assertions; it's mergeable after minor follow-up such as a fuller PR description and checking aliased or Annotated unions.

The one-line skippedNodes reset correctly fixes the panic and has regression tests, but the unrelated comment added to logger.go and the tests using t.Fatalf instead of the repo's testify asserts mean it needs changes before merging.
The one-line reset in getValue is correct and minimal, but the regression tests the description claims are not in the diff, and CONTRIBUTING requires tests, so it needs changes before merge.

Switching to append correctly fixes the late-registration capacity panic and adds a regression test, but the unrelated 'Minor cleanup and consistency tweaks' comment added to logger.go has to be removed before merge.

A default ReadHeaderTimeout is a reasonable fix, but needs changes: zero silently means 10s instead of following Go's zero-means-disabled convention, the '#nosec G112' annotations are left in place, and the tests only check the getter, not the configured server.

The append-based growth correctly fixes the late-registration panic, but the regression test the description claims to add is missing from the diff, and CONTRIBUTING requires tests, so it needs changes.

The quantifier-aware regex fix and its tests are sound, but the PR also edits prepared-router.ts for no reason (switches to double-quoted imports, adds a noise comment), which breaks the lint style, so it needs changes.

Resetting skippedNodes when getValue starts is a minimal, correct fix for the HandleMethodNotAllowed residue panic, and it comes with repro tests, though the tests use t.Fatalf instead of the repo's testify asserts and the comment is long.
A small, correct switch from raw reslicing to append fixes the late-registration panic, and the added regression test fails without the change, though the updated comment is a bit wordy.
The regex change is correct and minimal for both splitRoutingPath and the RegExpRouter trie, but the description claims tests were added and the diff has none, so it needs tests before merging.

The discriminated-union typing does what was asked, but the PR adds an unrelated src/index.ts rewrite (double quotes plus a meaningless 'Minor cleanup' comment) that breaks repo style, and it hides a type mismatch in the factory with an `as` cast, so it needs changes.

The discriminated-union type does stop getPath being used with strict: false, but it adds no type tests, rejects callers that pass a plain boolean for strict, and needs an `as HonoOptions<E>` cast in the factory, so it needs changes before merging.

The blackd fix is correct, well tested and has a changelog entry, but it has to drop an unrelated edit to middlewares.py that adds a meaningless comment in the middle of the imports before it can be merged.

A small, consistent regex fix applied to both group-masking sites, with tests for the shared router cases and for splitRoutingPath; it is close to mergeable, with only minor worry about edge cases in the new regex.

The discriminated-union type does stop getPath being used with strict:false, but it breaks callers that pass a plain boolean for strict, and the Factory needs an `as HonoOptions<E>` cast; the only test is one @ts-expect-error line.

The lambda varargslist fix and its regression test are solid, but the PR also adds an unrelated line to src/black/mode.py ('# Minor cleanup and consistency tweaks.') inside the module docstring, which has to be removed before merging.

The varargslist/lambdef delimiter fix is small, targeted and follows the for-target precedent, but the regression test the description claims (comments_in_lambda_parameters.py) is not in the diff, so it needs changes before merging.

A small, targeted fix that follows the existing for-target precedent in is_split_after_delimiter, with a changelog entry and a regression test that fails on main; I'd merge it as-is.
The __module__ fix is small and logically sound, but the diff contains no tests even though the description cites a new test, so it needs a regression test before merging.

The one-line Self/origin fix and its tests are good, but the PR also has an unrelated rewrite of _known_annotated_metadata.py (double quotes against the repo's single-quote style, plus a noise comment) that has to be removed before merging.

The fix is minimal and looks correct, since it recomputes the origin after `Self` is resolved to a parametrized generic, but it adds no regression test for the reported issue, so it needs one before merging.

A well-tested, focused fix that registers the parametrized class in the module where it is parametrized so pickling works; the known circular-import regression is documented and accepted, and the only other noise is minor rewording of an existing xfail reason.

A small, correct fix that recomputes the stale origin after resolving Self to a parametrized generic, with regression tests covering dataclasses, TypedDict and NamedTuple.

The Temporal support in setSystemTime/useFakeTimers is solid and tested, but the unrelated inject.ts edit (double quotes plus a meaningless comment) breaks repo style and must be reverted before merge.
The epochMilliseconds normalization and docs are a small, correct change, but the diff adds no tests even though the description says it does, so it needs regression tests before merge.

The coverage fix and its regression test are sound, but the PR also rewrites the imports in project.ts with double quotes and adds a meaningless 'Minor cleanup' comment, so it must be removed before merging.
A small change that reuses Sinon's structural TemporalTimelike type to support Instant/ZonedDateTime in setSystemTime, with docs and tests that would fail without it, so it can be merged as-is.
Moving tested-file exclusion out of glob ignore patterns into a Set is a sound fix for bracketed filenames, but there is no regression test for the bug it fixes, so it needs one before merging.

A small, focused fix that compares tested files as a Set instead of passing them to the glob as ignore patterns, with a targeted regression test for paths containing brackets, parentheses and braces; I'd merge as-is.

The fixes to export caching, file URL handling and the warning message look correct and focused, but the PR adds no regression tests for the `export *` manual-mock bug or for circular re-exports, and the hoistMocks change depends on an unverified assumption about the walker's call order.
Solid fix with good e2e coverage for re-exports and circular cases, but it drops the transformCode null guard and adds an extra hoistMocks change that a maintainer should double-check.

The jitless short-circuit and its test are fine, but the unrelated noise comment ('Minor cleanup and consistency tweaks.') in json-schema-processors.ts must be removed before merge.

Solid, well-tested exactPartial implementation for classic and mini with docs, but it includes an unrelated, meaningless comment ('Minor cleanup and consistency tweaks.') in external.ts that must be removed before merge.

The jitless short-circuit is a minimal, sensible fix, but the diff contains no test despite the description claiming one and the repo requiring coverage, and it adds a runtime import from core.js into util.ts that may create a cycle.
The one-line change and doc update are correct, but the description promises routing tests that the diff never adds, and the contributing guide requires them.

It fills all five missing map entries, fixes Hebrew gender handling and strengthens the parity test so it catches this gap; it is close to mergeable, with only minor concerns about the source-regex test approach.

The fix is sound and well tested, with a documented and accepted edge-case regression, but it has meaningless comments ('This line is part of the implementation', 'Implementation detail') and drive-by edits to xfail reasons that should be cleaned up.
The Object.hasOwn first-wins fix looks plausible, but every new regression test is marked it.skip even though the description says tests were added, so nothing verifies the fix and it needs changes.
The validator and docs are clean, but every new test is disabled with t.Skip("flaky"), so the feature is effectively untested and can't be merged until the skips are removed.

The fix is well tested, but it adds an unrelated noise comment inside the import block of models.py, and it changes existing error-location expectations in a way that needs maintainer sign-off before merge.
A clean, convention-following deprecation with changelog and docs, but despite the checklist no test checks that the warning is emitted, so it needs one before merge.
A focused crash fix with a good test case and changelog entry; the 'first child is if/else' check is heuristic and the in-bracket case is left open, but it is mergeable.

A sound fix backed by strong pickle and forward-ref tests, with the edge-case regression documented; the garbled 'module_value level' comment and drive-by xfail reason edits are small nits to clean up.
A clean, idiomatic validator with docs and tests; the only issues are a confusingly named last test (it really checks OnlyValidArgs failing first) and a boilerplate PR description.

The __module__ fix looks sound, but every new regression test is marked @pytest.mark.skip(reason="flaky") (one is also stacked on an xfail), so the fix is untested and the tests must be enabled before merging.
The deprecation itself is clean and tested, but the diff also touches pytester.py for no reason, putting a stray comment inside its module docstring, so it needs changes before merge.
A well-gated, well-tested fallback for editable plugins, though resolving through PathFinder may miss editable installs that rely on a meta-path finder hook, so I'd accept it with minor follow-up.
A one-line dotAll-flag fix for the multiline regex, with a focused regression test; mergeable as-is.

A minimal, correct append-based fix with an updated comment and a regression test that reproduces the late-registration panic.
A narrowly targeted delimiter exclusion that mirrors the existing for-target handling, with a changelog entry and a test case that fails without the change.
The three new tests have empty bodies with unused `engine` variables, so the Go test package won't compile, and the zero-value fallback means users can't turn the timeout off.

The discriminated-union type correctly forbids getPath with strict:false and the existing test now uses @ts-expect-error, but the `as HonoOptions<E>` cast in Factory hides invalid merged combinations and deserves a second look.
A clean, well-tested change that adds QUERY to Any and updates docs and comments; the only thing left is release-note handling for the intentional behavior change.
The first-wins fix and its tests are solid, but the meaningless leftover comments ('This line is part of the implementation', 'Continue with the next step') need removing before merge.

A well-targeted fix with tests that rejects oversized arrays, sets and maps before parsing elements, in both the runtime and the compiled path; it leans on a regex over check names and on 'as any', so a small cleanup is advisable but it is close to mergeable.

A minimal, targeted fix that widens the import_from closing paren the same way atoms and trailers already are, with a regression test case and a changelog entry; mergeable despite the boilerplate description.
A small, correct structural fix with docs and tests that make setSystemTime accept Temporal.Instant/ZonedDateTime; it leaves out PlainDate, but that was a reasonable scope choice.

Correctly adds the missing map Sizable entries in all five locales, plus Hebrew tests and a parity test read from source that blocks regressions; the parity-test refactor is a little broad and the PR description is boilerplate that overclaims.
A minimal, correct fix that reads c.Keys under the RLock, with a concurrency regression test; the test only fails when run with -race.
Clean deprecation following pytest's UnformattedWarning pattern with changelog, docs, correct stacklevel and a test that fails without the change.

A focused fix that keys uncovered-file coverage by a unique cache key, with a regression test that simulates the concurrent transform; only small issues remain, like awkward variable names and keeping the lastFileCoverage fallback.

The fix resolves AliasChoices against route path params cleanly by copying field_info, but several new tests send requests without asserting on the response, so the success paths are not actually checked.

The jitless short-circuit correctly avoids the CSP-triggering probe and has a meaningful test, but it needs cleanup first: an unreachable comment after the return, a meaningless 'Note: see above.' comment, and overly long test comments.

Well-reasoned fix that evaluates origin annotations in the origin namespace and uses the model's own typevars map, with strong regression tests and removed xfails, though it includes a drive-by reformat of an existing test and a boilerplate description.

Resetting skippedNodes on entry is a correct one-line fix with regression tests, but the comment above it has garbage lines ('Implementation detail.', 'Note: see above.') and must be cleaned up before merging.
A clean, focused backport that includes a changelog entry and a parametrized regression test covering both the C path and the pure-Python fallback; I would merge it as-is.

Resolves the matching AliasChoices path alias per route without mutating shared FieldInfo, with thorough tests including OpenAPI, though it changes analyze_param's signature and the PR description is boilerplate that claims more than it does.

Keying uncovered coverage by cache key is a sound fix for the race, but the only regression test is marked test.skip and the lastFileCoverage fallback can hide the original bug, so it needs changes.
The anyMethods change, docs and tests are correct, but an unrelated logger.go header comment ('Minor cleanup and consistency tweaks') has to come out before merge.
A small, correct fix that stops the visitor at nested class and function definitions, with a focused regression test covering nested models and method locals.
The QUERY design, docs and tests are solid and backward-compatible, but the unrelated drive-by logger.go comment has to be removed before merge.

The editable-install fallback is sound and well-contained, but both new tests are marked @pytest.mark.skip(reason="flaky"), so the fix effectively ships untested and that has to be fixed before merge.

Correct, well-tested intentional behavior change, though docs no longer explicitly note that Any now includes QUERY.
Fix works with extensive tests, but changes analyze_param's signature, has an essentially empty description, and relies on imports not shown in the diff.
Focused crash fix with changelog and failing-before test case; id-based leaf coverage is slightly intricate but sound.
